meta.description: Numori is a family of open-source apps and services — notes, mail, calendar, files and more — built for privacy, free of AI features, and priced as one fair subscription.

hero.eyebrow: Every line of it open source
hero.title: Software that minds its own business
hero.subtitle: Notes, mail, calendar, files, tasks and more. Built properly, priced fairly, and with no interest whatsoever in what you keep inside them.
hero.note: No AI assistants. No tracking. No adverts. Not now, not later.

principles.title: What we actually promise
principles.subtitle: Six commitments. Each one is either visible in the source code or it is not a commitment at all.

private.title: Private by design
private.body: No tracking, no profiling, no advertising, no third-party analytics. Each service collects what it technically needs to function, and stops there.

open.title: Open source, all of it
open.body: Every client and every server, not just the bits that are safe to show. Promises are cheap; a public repository you can compile yourself is not.

noAi.title: No AI, anywhere
noAi.body: No assistants, no summaries, no "smart" suggestions quietly reading your data to justify a valuation. Tools that do the thing you asked, and only that.

priced.title: Priced like a utility
priced.body: One modest subscription covers the entire ecosystem. No per-product tiers, no per-seat arithmetic, no "contact sales".

craft.title: Craft over churn
craft.body: Small, careful releases. Keyboard-first, properly accessible, quick on the hardware you already own, and translated by people who speak the language.

portable.title: Yours to take
portable.body: Open formats and one-click export in every app. Self-host the whole stack, or walk out with your data intact. Leaving should be boring.

products.title: One ecosystem, not a bundle of acquisitions
products.subtitle: Everything shares one account, one design system and one set of rules. Here are the pieces we are building first.

notes.tagline: Notes that do the maths for you
notes.summary: A plain-text notepad with a natural-language calculator built into every line. Write "48 GBP in EUR" or "12% of 340" and the answer appears beside it, no separate calculator needed.

1.title: A calculator that reads English
1.body: Units, currencies, percentages, SI prefixes and variables, all in the same line of prose you were already typing.

2.title: Local first, sync optional
2.body: Notes live on your device and stay there. Turn on end-to-end encrypted sync only if you want them on a second device.

3.title: Exports that are not a hostage negotiation
3.body: Markdown, plain text, DOCX and PDF, all from a menu rather than a support request.

4.title: Genuinely offline
4.body: The desktop and mobile apps bundle everything they need. No network, no degraded mode.

clips.tagline: A clipboard with a memory and a filter
clips.summary: A clipboard manager that keeps your history on your machine, recognises code and formats it properly, and refuses to record anything from the apps you tell it to ignore.

1.title: Nothing leaves the device by default
1.body: History is stored locally. Sync is opt-in, end-to-end encrypted, and can be turned off without losing what you already have.

2.title: An ignore list that is actually respected
2.body: Name your password manager, your banking app, your terminal. Clips will not record from them, full stop.

3.title: Understands code
3.body: Snippets are detected, syntax-highlighted and pasted back with their formatting intact.

4.title: Locks like a phone
4.body: PIN, password or biometrics, plus a privacy screen so your history is not in the app switcher.

mail.summary: An encrypted mailbox with no assistant offering to write your replies and no engine reading your post to sell you a holiday. Standard protocols, open formats, your own domain.

1.title: Nothing reads your mail
1.body: No summarising, no smart replies, no categorising by content. The only party parsing your messages is your own client.

2.title: Encrypted where it counts
2.body: End-to-end encryption between Numori accounts, and standards-based encryption with everyone else.

3.title: Your domain, your addresses
3.body: Custom domains, generous aliases and per-sender addresses included, not sold as an add-on.

4.title: No lock-in at the protocol level
4.body: IMAP and SMTP access, full mailbox export, and an importer that gets you in without a migration project.

drive.tagline: Storage that cannot read what it stores
drive.summary: End-to-end encrypted file storage with ordinary sharing, ordinary folders and no content scanning. Files go up encrypted, and the server never sees the keys.

1.title: Encrypted before it leaves
1.body: Encryption happens on your device. We hold ciphertext and metadata we cannot avoid, and nothing else.

2.title: Sharing without an account requirement
2.body: Password-protected, expiring links that work for people who will never sign up to anything.

3.title: Versions and a real bin
3.body: File history and a recovery window, because "encrypted" should not mean "one mistake from gone".

4.title: Sync that behaves
4.body: Selective sync, sensible conflict handling and no surprise re-uploads of your entire library.

calendar.tagline: A calendar that keeps your schedule to itself
calendar.summary: Encrypted events with proper recurrence, real time-zone handling and invitations that work with everyone else's calendar. Your diary is not training data.

1.title: Encrypted event contents
1.body: Titles, locations, notes and guests are encrypted. What we can see is limited to what scheduling technically requires.

2.title: Recurrence that survives reality
2.body: Exceptions, moved instances and cross-time-zone repeats handled correctly, including the awkward ones.

3.title: Works with the outside world
3.body: CalDAV, ICS subscriptions and standard invitations, so nobody has to join anything to meet you.

4.title: Availability sharing without exposure
4.body: Share that you are busy without sharing what you are doing.

tasks.summary: Lists, projects, due dates and recurrence, with an offline-first store and keyboard-first navigation. No streaks, no scoring, no nudges.

1.title: Keyboard-first throughout
1.body: Add, schedule, reorder and complete without touching the mouse. Every action has a shortcut.

2.title: Offline by default
2.body: The list is on your device. Sync is a feature you enable, not a dependency you inherit.

3.title: No gamification
3.body: No streaks to break, no productivity score, no notifications engineered to pull you back in.

4.title: Fits the rest of the suite
4.body: Tasks reference notes and calendar entries directly, without a third-party integration in the middle.

chat.tagline: Messaging with nothing in the middle
chat.summary: End-to-end encrypted conversations for one-to-one and groups, with metadata kept to the bare minimum and no bots reading the room.

1.title: Encrypted by default, not on request
1.body: Every conversation, including groups, with no downgrade path and no "secret chat" toggle to forget.

2.title: Minimal metadata
2.body: We are designing to hold as little as possible about who talks to whom, and to document exactly what remains.

3.title: No assistants in your conversations
3.body: No suggested replies, no summarising of what you missed, no third party parsing the transcript.

4.title: Self-hostable
4.body: Run the server yourself and federate, or keep a group entirely inside your own infrastructure.

marks.summary: Encrypted bookmarks with full-text search, archived copies of what you saved, and a browser extension that does not phone home about your browsing.

1.title: The extension collects nothing
1.body: It saves what you ask it to save. It does not report the pages you visit, ever.

2.title: Keeps a copy
2.body: Optional readable snapshots, so a dead link is an inconvenience rather than a loss.

3.title: Search that reaches inside
3.body: Full-text search across the pages you saved, not just their titles and tags.

4.title: Imports and exports plainly
4.body: Standard bookmark files in and out. Bring the pile you have accumulated elsewhere.

sheets.summary: A fast, collaborative spreadsheet with a familiar formula language, encrypted documents and no assistant guessing at your intent.

1.title: Formulas you already know
1.body: A compatible formula language, so existing sheets and existing habits both survive the move.

2.title: Collaboration without a middleman
2.body: Real-time editing over the same encrypted sync layer the rest of the suite uses.

3.title: Quick on large sheets
3.body: Built for tens of thousands of rows without the tab becoming unresponsive.

4.title: Open formats both ways
4.body: Native ODS and XLSX import and export, plus CSV for everything else.

forms.tagline: Forms that do not surveil respondents
forms.summary: Build a form, share a link, collect encrypted responses. No trackers embedded in the page, no analytics on the people filling it in.

1.title: Encrypted responses
1.body: Answers are encrypted to you. The service stores submissions it cannot read.

2.title: No tracking in the form itself
2.body: No third-party scripts, no fingerprinting, no IP logging beyond what abuse prevention needs.

3.title: Accessible out of the box
3.body: Keyboard navigable, screen-reader tested, and readable at 200% zoom without you configuring anything.

4.title: Results where you want them
4.body: Export to CSV, or push straight into a Numori Sheets document.

finance.tagline: Budgeting that stays on your device
finance.summary: Track accounts, budgets and spending with everything encrypted and nothing shared. No bank scraping, no data brokers, no offers based on your balance.

1.title: No third-party bank connections
1.body: Import statements yourself. We will not hand your credentials to an aggregator that resells the transaction feed.

2.title: Multi-currency arithmetic that works
2.body: Built on the same calculation engine as Numori Notes, including historical rates.

3.title: Nobody sells you anything
3.body: No sponsored products, no credit-score upsells, no referral commission shaping the advice.

4.title: Reports you can take away
4.body: CSV, ODS and PDF exports, plus a full encrypted backup on request.

pdf.tagline: PDF tools that never see your document
pdf.summary: Merge, split, sign, compress and convert entirely in your browser or on your desktop. Files are not uploaded, because the processing happens locally.

1.title: Nothing is uploaded
1.body: Every operation runs on your own machine. There is no server to trust with the contract you are signing.

2.title: The whole toolbox
2.body: Merge, split, rotate, reorder, compress, redact, sign and fill in forms.

3.title: Redaction that actually removes
3.body: Redacted content is deleted from the file, not covered with a black rectangle you can drag away.

4.title: Works offline
4.body: Install it once and it keeps working on a train, on a plane, and on a locked-down network.

auth.summary: The identity service behind every Numori product: sign-in, sessions, devices and recovery. Open source, self-hostable, and deliberately boring.

1.title: One account, every product
1.body: Sign in once. No separate registration per app, and no separate password to lose.

2.title: Strong second factors
2.body: Passkeys, hardware keys and TOTP. Recovery codes you print, not a phone number we can be socially engineered out of.

3.title: Sessions you can see
3.body: Every active device listed, with one-tap revocation and a readable log of sign-ins.

4.title: Standards, not a walled garden
4.body: OAuth 2.1 and OpenID Connect, so you can put your own applications behind it too.

crdt.tagline: The sync layer, and it cannot read a thing
crdt.summary: The conflict-free replication service every Numori app syncs through. It relays encrypted changes between your devices without ever holding a key.

1.title: Zero-knowledge relay
1.body: The server moves encrypted operations around. It has no keys and therefore no view of your content.

2.title: Merges without losing edits
2.body: Conflict-free replicated data types, so two offline devices reconcile cleanly instead of picking a winner.

3.title: Offline is the normal case
3.body: Edit for a week with no connection. Reconnecting is a merge, not a conflict-resolution interview.

4.title: Run your own
4.body: A single container, documented configuration, and clients that will happily point at your server instead of ours.

pulse.tagline: Status and uptime, out in the open
pulse.summary: The public health dashboard for every Numori service, plus the monitoring behind it. Incidents are posted while they are happening, not summarised afterwards.

1.title: Honest incident history
1.body: Nothing is quietly edited later. Past incidents stay published, with what broke and what we changed.

2.title: No third-party status vendor
2.body: The status page does not embed someone else's tracking script to tell you our servers are up.

3.title: Subscribe how you like
3.body: Email, RSS or webhooks. No account needed to be told a service is down.

4.title: Useful on its own
4.body: Self-host it to monitor your own services. It is a real monitoring tool, not a marketing page.

updater.tagline: Updates that do not report back
updater.summary: The release and update service for the desktop and mobile apps. It ships signed builds and learns as little as possible about the machines it updates.

1.title: Signed and verifiable
1.body: Every build is signed and reproducible, so you can confirm the binary matches the public source.

2.title: Update checks are not telemetry
2.body: The check asks for a version number. It does not carry a device profile or a persistent identifier.

3.title: You choose when
3.body: Automatic, prompted or manual. Nothing installs itself in the middle of your work.

4.title: Roll back cleanly
4.body: Previous versions stay available and downgrading is supported, because releases are occasionally wrong.

ui.tagline: The design system behind all of it
ui.summary: The Tailwind 4 and Vue 3 component library every Numori interface is built from. Accessible, tree-shakeable, and usable in your own projects.

1.title: Accessibility is not a variant
1.body: Keyboard behaviour, focus management and ARIA semantics are part of each component, not a prop you remember to set.

2.title: Take only what you use
2.body: Import a single component and ship a few kilobytes. Nothing drags the whole library along.

3.title: Nuxt module or Vite plugin
3.body: Auto-import in Nuxt, a resolver in plain Vite, or explicit imports anywhere else.

4.title: Documented in the source
4.body: Every component carries its props, events, slots and examples in JSDoc, so your editor already knows the API.

template.tagline: The starting point for a Numori app
template.summary: The project scaffold every Numori application begins from: Nuxt, the design system, i18n, linting, testing and release wiring already agreed upon.

1.title: Decisions already made
1.body: Linting, formatting, hooks, testing and CI configured the way the rest of the ecosystem is configured.

2.title: Every target from day one
2.body: Web, desktop and mobile builds wired up before you write a line of product code.

3.title: Translatable from the first commit
3.body: i18n structure in place, so localisation is never a retrofit.

4.title: Useful outside Numori
4.body: None of it is specific to us. Clone it for your own privacy-respecting application.

meta.title: Pricing
meta.description: One low subscription for the entire Numori ecosystem, a free tier that is genuinely useful, and self-hosting that costs nothing.

pricing.title: One price, everything in it
pricing.subtitle: No per-product tiers, no seat maths, no enterprise phone call. The free tier is not a trial, and self-hosting is not a downgrade.

draftNotice.title: These numbers are not final
draftNotice.body: Most of the ecosystem is still being built, so treat this page as our intent. We will publish final pricing before anyone is asked to pay, and we will not raise it on people who signed up earlier.

features.2: Local storage with no size limit

complete.name: Complete
complete.tagline: The whole ecosystem, one line on your statement

features.4: Custom domains and aliases in Mail
features.5: Priority support from the people who wrote it

features.2: No licence fee and no user cap

1.a: Because we are not funding a sales team, an advertising budget or a data-science department. A small, well-run ecosystem does not need thirty pounds a month from you to survive.

2.q: What happens if Numori shuts down?
2.a: Everything is AGPL-3.0 and self-hostable, and every app exports to open formats. If we disappear, you can run the whole stack yourself or take your data elsewhere. That is the point of publishing the servers too.

3.q: Will you add AI features later once it gets expensive not to?
3.a: No. It is a founding commitment rather than a current preference, and it is the sort of promise that is easy to check: watch the repositories.

4.q: Is the free tier just a trial?
4.a: No. It has no expiry and it includes every application. The paid tier buys hosted sync and storage, not the software itself.

5.q: Do you offer student or non-profit pricing?
5.a: Yes, once billing exists. It will be a straightforward discount rather than an application process.

meta.title: About and manifesto
meta.description: Why Numori exists: an open-source, privacy-first, deliberately AI-free alternative to software that treats its users as inventory.

about.title: Why we are building this
about.subtitle: A short manifesto, and the reasoning we keep coming back to.
about.intro: Most software you rely on is engineered around a business model that needs your attention or your data. Numori is an attempt to build the same tools around a much duller model: you pay a small amount, we run the service well, and nothing else happens.

1.title: Privacy is an architecture, not a policy page
1.body: A privacy policy is a promise about what a company will choose to do. Encryption and local-first storage are statements about what it is able to do. We prefer the second kind and design so that the tempting option is not technically available to us.

2.title: Open source has to include the servers
2.body: Publishing a client while the server stays closed proves very little: the interesting decisions happen where you cannot see them. Every Numori server is public under the AGPL-3.0, which is why we can reasonably ask to be trusted, and why you do not have to.

3.title: Refusing AI is a feature
3.body: We are not against the technology in the abstract. We are against what it currently requires: your private data moved somewhere it can be processed, a running cost that has to be recovered from you, and a category of feature nobody asked for arriving switched on. So there is none of it, anywhere, and there will not be.

4.title: Software should be finished, not fed
4.body: A note-taking app does not need a quarterly redesign. We would rather ship fewer, better-considered releases and spend the difference on correctness, accessibility and speed than manufacture activity to look alive.

5.title: Accessibility is not an extra
5.body: Keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, sensible contrast, reduced-motion handling and real translations are part of the definition of finished. If it only works for someone using a mouse, with perfect vision, in English, it is not finished.

6.title: Fair price, no dark patterns
6.body: One price for everything, cancellation that takes one click, no countdown timers, no interstitials asking whether you are sure you want to leave, and no price rise aimed at people already signed up.

7.title: Leaving should be easy
7.body: Every app exports everything, in formats other software can read, without a support ticket. If we have to trap you to keep you, we have already failed at the actual job.

who.title: Who is building it
who.body: A very small team, working carefully rather than quickly. Numori is developed in the open by Erik Bjerke with Yaiza Wadhwani Valderas and TheProcedural Software Ltd, and every repository takes contributions.

openSource.subtitle: Nineteen repositories under the AGPL-3.0. Clients, servers, the design system and the website you are reading.

licence.title: Why the AGPL-3.0
licence.body: The AGPL closes the loophole that lets a hosted service build on open code without giving anything back. Anyone may run, modify and offer Numori as a service; they simply have to publish their changes too. It keeps the ecosystem open even if we are no longer the ones maintaining it.

contribute.title: Contributing
contribute.body: Issues, translations, accessibility audits and pull requests are all welcome. Translation work is especially valuable: we would rather ship a language properly than run machine translation over the interface.
